prerequisites: No prior courses are required, though it relies on basic knowledge and competencies acquired in previous years.
Basic computer literacy for user-level personal computer handling is highly recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals and applications of digital electronics and microprocessors.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students are able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the capacity to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

teaching_methods: Participation of the teaching team and support tutors
Use of basic bibliography and complementary material
Compulsory practical assignments involving prior simulation exercises
In-person practical activities in ETSI Industriales laboratories

assessment_methods.method: In-person Mixed Exam (5 short theoretical-practical questions, 2 problems)
Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC I and PEC II)
Distance and In-person Laboratory Practices (simulation and hands-on assembly)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 70% from the in-person mixed exam, 10% from the Continuous Assessment Tests (PECs), and 20% from the distance and in-person laboratory practices. To pass the in-person exam, a minimum of 2 points must be obtained in each of its parts (short questions and problems), and a minimum total score of 4 out of 10 is required for the PEC and practice grades to be considered. Incorrect answers in test questions will be penalized by 50% of their value. Laboratory practices are compulsory and must be passed to clear the course; if passed, they do not need to be redone in subsequent attempts. Ordinary exam sessions are in February (students choose one of two weeks), with an extraordinary session in September; reserve exams are possible under UNED regulations.
